flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e6 is the strongest move because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: e6 does not pressure anything yet. It prepares ...d5, which is the whole point of the French. Calling it the strongest move because of 'center pressure' is the same sentence you used on e4, just shuffled. I already know pawns go toward the middle; tell me this is the French.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your e-pawn is the strongest move.
flags.critique: d5 is defended by the e6 pawn, so the hanging/doubled/backward tags on this capture are junk. Exchange French is a choice, not a tactic. Nc3, e5, and Nd2 are all normal here. You sold a structure decision as if I won a loose pawn.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your e-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: This is a recapture. I am restoring material, not winning an undefended pawn. wins_material on this ply is a lie. If you cannot say 'you recapture so you are not down a pawn,' stay quiet rather than invent a free lunch.

flags.quote: Moving your c8-bishop to f5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: In a French the c8 bishop is the problem child. Getting it to f5 before it gets locked in is the reason Black is happy in the Exchange. You gave me 'development' and 'That's the one.' I learned nothing I would not get from a random Nf6.

flags.quote: Moving your b8-knight to d7 is a mistake, but moving your f8-bishop to e7 would be better because you can likely take a bishop.
flags.critique: Be7 does not take a bishop. The real problem is Nxd5: f6 is pinned to the queen by Bg5, so the d5 pawn is only pretending to be defended. Nbd7 walks into that shot. Teach the pin, not a made-up capture from three moves down a PV.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-bishop to d3 is a mistake, but taking the pawn on d5 with your c3-knight would be better because you can likely fork the black king and the black d7-knight and then take a knight.
flags.critique: A knight on d5 does not attack the king on e8 or the knight on d7. That fork is geometrically false. Nxd5 wins because Nf6 is pinned: ...Nfxd5 loses the queen to Bxd8, and ...Ndxd5 drops a pawn after Bxf6. Lichess called this an inaccuracy and you called it a mistake, then explained the wrong tactic.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d3 with your f5-bishop is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Bd3 is defended by the c-pawn. This is a trade, not a hanging-piece win. You tagged hanging anyway and then had nothing to say. At least mention I am swapping the active French bishop for White's light-squared bishop.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d3 with your c-pawn is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: Of course I recapture the bishop that just took on d3. wins_material is wrong; I am not gaining a piece. The thing a 1200 might actually miss is that cxd3 doubles the d-pawns and opens the c-file, and you had those tags sitting unused.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to d6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You lost 40 centipawns and still said strongest, with an empty reason list. Bd6 aims at h2, which is the plan that later wins the game. 'Strongest' with no idea attached is just a stamp.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-rook to e1 is playable, but taking the pawn on d5 with your c3-knight would be better because you can likely pin the knight to the queen.
flags.critique: The pin already exists. Bg5 has been pinning Nf6 since move 6. Nxd5 uses that pin; it does not create one. Third time this game you have the right move (Nxd5) and a fake because-clause. I am going to start ignoring your 'likely' sentences.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: c6 finally puts a second, unpinned defender on d5 so Nxd5 stops working. You spent three notes failing to explain that tactic, then skipped the move that kills it. Empty strongest again.

flags.quote: Moving your f3-knight to e5 is the strongest move because it gives your king better protection and it gives your knight a strong outpost.
flags.critique: Ne5 does not protect my king. Outpost is the real word. Gluing on 'king better protection' makes me distrust the outpost claim too, even though that one is fair.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to c7 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Queen on c7 and bishop on d6 is a battery pointed at h2. That is the setup for Bxh2+ later. You had a blank reason list and a gold-star quip. Teach the battery.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a3 leaves your e5-knight hanging to the black d7-knight and bishop. A better move would have been moving your a1-rook to c1 because your rook can use a semi-open file.
flags.critique: You correctly named the hanging knight, then recommended Rc1, which also does not save it. So I am supposed to lose the pawn anyway, but with a rook on a semi-open file? If the engine move ignores the threat you just named, say that. Do not change the subject to files.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e5 with your d7-knight is the strongest move because you come out a pawn ahead.
flags.critique: On this ply I traded knight for knight. The extra pawn appears after dxe5 Bxe5. Saying I am already a pawn up mid-exchange is the SEE lookahead talking, not a lesson. king_safer on a knight trade is extra noise.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e5 with your d-pawn is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead and you take the defender of the black bishop.
flags.critique: I recaptured a knight with a pawn. I am not a bishop ahead. The knight on e5 is not defending Black's bishop on d6. This is the worst sentence in the game so far: two false claims glued together on a recapture.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e5 with your bishop is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: The pawn I took is the white pawn. I cannot also 'take the defender of the white pawn' in the same breath. I am a pawn up because e5 was hanging after the knight recapture. Say that. The removed_defender line is word salad.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: d4 hits the bishop on e5 with a pawn tempo. That is a kick, and you even tagged ignored_threat on a best move, which is backwards. Tell me I am attacking the bishop. 'Strongest move' with no because is filler.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on h2 with your bishop is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: It is check. The bishop was hanging to d4 and I took h2 with check instead of retreating. That is the whole idea: zwischenzug, not 'undefended pawn.' You had back_rank and saves_piece in the tags and still taught the recapture template. I would have learned more from a puzzle book caption.

flags.quote: Moving your king to h1 is the strongest move because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: The question a beginner actually has is why not take the bishop. Kxh2 runs into Ng4+ and the queen coming to h2. pawn_shield after the h-pawn is gone is a joke. 'Keeps your king safer' does not tell me what I was refusing.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to f4 is playable, but moving your bishop to d6 would be better because you can likely take a bishop.
flags.critique: Bd6 does not take a bishop. Same 'likely take' lie as Be7 on move 12. Bf4 offers a trade; Bd6 keeps the piece and the battery. If you do not know why the engine likes Bd6, do not invent a capture.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on f4 with your bishop puts it where the black queen can take and you lose a knight.
flags.critique: I recaptured a bishop. The queen taking on f4 is the recapture, not a knight win. You are labeling a 300-centipawn SEE as 'a knight' while I still have Nc3. The real punch is that Qxf4 becomes a monster and Bxf6 was the way to wreck the kingside instead.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your e1-rook to e3 leaves your pawn hanging to the black queen.
flags.critique: Which pawn? f2 is the one Qf4 actually eyes, and the king is on h1 so it is not obvious. The Qf3 skewer behind this is the one sentence in the game that taught a real tactic. Name the square.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to g4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Ng4 and Qf4 threaten Qh2 mate. This is the move of the game and you wrote a blank strongest-move sticker. If you cannot say 'you threaten mate on h2,' you should not be coaching this position.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your queen to e2 lets black force checkmate in 1 move. This lets black force checkmate in 1 move. A better move would have been taking the knight on g4 with your queen because you pin the pawn to the king.
flags.critique: You said mate in one twice, then explained Qxg4 as pinning a pawn to the king. Qxg4 takes the piece that covers h2 so Qh2# is not mate. I needed 'take the mating knight,' not a pin story, and I did not need the same sentence copied under itself.

suggestions.title: Stop calling recaptures material wins
suggestions.detail: wins_material fires when capturedSeeCp >= 80, so taking back on d5/e5/d3 becomes 'undefended' or 'a bishop ahead.' Gate it: if the captured unit arrived on that square last ply, emit recapture, not wins_material. A 1200 knows they recaptured; they get angry when you say they won a piece. Fixes plies 6, 15, 24, 25, 26.

suggestions.title: Name captures that work because a defender is pinned
suggestions.detail: Nxd5 is the lesson of this French and the coach never said pin. Add an exploits_pin reason when a capture's SEE is good only because a defender (here Nf6) is pinned to a higher piece. Surface that instead of PV forks/pins/captures. Would have fixed the Nbd7/Bd3/Re1 cluster with one detector.

suggestions.title: Do not teach 'likely take' from later PV noise
suggestions.detail: verifyLikelyTactics keeps likely:true captures/pins/forks whenever evalLoss >= 80, even if they happen on ply 2–4 of the improvement line. That produced 'likely take a bishop' (Be7, Bd6), a fake king+d7 fork, and 'likely pin' on a pin that already exists. Only allow likely tactics from the first ply of the suggested line, or drop them from the because-clause.

suggestions.title: Lead with check when the move is check
suggestions.detail: selectBecauseReasons prefers capture/wins_material over check, so Bxh2+ became 'the pawn was undefended.' Rank check (and saves_piece when the moving piece was hanging) above recapture copy. Optional kicked_by_pawn-as-benefit on the previous d4 would let you say the bishop took h2 with check instead of retreating.

suggestions.title: Stop mate-in-1 twice; say the better move stops mate
suggestions.detail: allows_mate is both problem and consequence; containsIgnoreCase uses the first 24 chars of the consequence, so 'this lets black force…' does not match 'lets black force…' and the sentence duplicates. Skip consequence when it restates allows_mate. For the suggested move, if the played move allows mate, the because should be stops_mate (Qxg4 removes the Qh2# cover), not a random pin from the PV. Also emit a mate_threat benefit on the attacking move (Ng4) so ply 34 is not blank.

suggestions.title: Call a hanging bishop a bishop
suggestions.detail: materialLabel maps 250–399cp to 'a knight', so a hanging bishop (300) on Bxf4 became 'you lose a knight.' hangingLossCopy should use the hanging unit's type, and only fall back to cp buckets when the SEE is a mix. A 1200 looking at the board sees a bishop recapture and thinks the coach cannot count pieces.

suggestions.title: Ban empty 'strongest move' on forcing ideas
suggestions.detail: c6, Qc7, d4, Ng4, Bd6 all printed 'is the strongest move.' with no because. If playedBenefits is empty, either pick a plan-level reason (stops a hanging capture, queen+bishop battery, pawn kick, mate threat) or downgrade the verdict to 'a normal useful move.' Outpost on Ne5 was good; king_safer on the same move was not. Gate king_safer unless the king actually moved or a check was blocked.

suggestions.title: If you name a hanging piece, the better move must address it
suggestions.detail: On a3 the problem was Ne5 hanging, then suggestedBecause was a semi-open file for Rc1, which also loses the knight. When the top problem is ignored_threat/hanging, prefer a suggested benefit that saves or recaptures that unit; if the engine move does not, say you still lose it and Rc1 is only the least-bad follow-up. Same rule would stop Qxg4 being sold as a pin-to-the-king while mate is on the board.

whatWorked: Bg5: 'you pin the knight to the queen' is the one opening sentence that taught a real idea.
Both castles: shelter plus rook toward the center is plain and true.
a3: correctly flagged Ne5 as hanging to knight and bishop, even if the improvement lecture wandered off.
Re3: the Qf3 skewer through queen to knight is real tactics, not PV fanfic.
Qe2: mate-in-1 detection fired (the duplicate and the pin-because then ruined it).
